name: Mojave 3
label: 4AD
lede: Creation dropped Slowdive a week after their third album, so three of them sent Ivo Watts-Russell a cassette of quiet acoustic songs and became a country-tinged 4AD band in the middle of Britpop.

hero.by: Neil Halstead, Rachel Goswell and Ian McCutcheon, 1995

eras.title: A demo tape after Slowdive
eras.text: Slowdive were finished at Creation Records, and Neil Halstead had been writing acoustic songs in his west London flat even while making the band's ambient last record. 4AD's founder, who had once wanted Slowdive, heard the demos and signed what was left.

years.src: Wikipedia: Ask Me Tomorrow · Wikipedia: Mojave 3
years.h: Creation drops Slowdive a week after Pygmalion
years.p: Halstead, [[Rachel Goswell|80e91439-21f6-4a0a-84f8-23be4cd48549]] and drummer [[Ian McCutcheon|1d54d158-0f51-4247-a674-e8ea24c6dd03]] are left with a pile of folk-leaning songs Halstead wrote alongside the album.

years.cap: Neil Halstead, Rachel Goswell and Ian McCutcheon in a 4AD promo print, 1995
years.src: 4AD: Ask Me Tomorrow · BrooklynVegan · Wikipedia: Mojave 3
years.h: Ivo Watts-Russell signs them off a six-track cassette
years.p: The 4AD founder had wanted to sign Slowdive. The trio's acoustic demos are enough, Britpop or not.
years.xp: 4AD's own notes describe a "bumptious Britpop" climate that "seemed totally at odds" with the band. They called themselves Mojave, found another band had the name, and added a 3 for the three of them.

years.cap: Halstead, Goswell and McCutcheon on a contact sheet, 1995
years.src: Wikipedia: Ask Me Tomorrow · 4AD: Ask Me Tomorrow
years.h: Ask Me Tomorrow barely changes the demos
years.p: Eight months after Pygmalion, in a Vaughan Oliver and Chris Bigg sleeve. Reviewers reach for Nick Drake, Cowboy Junkies and Dylan.

years.h: A Chapterhouse guitarist and a keyboard player make it five
years.p: [[Simon Rowe|05b4795f-ebea-47e5-bf4f-d163da6acccc]], formerly of Chapterhouse, and Alan Forrester join after the debut, which reaches the US in January.

eras.title: Pedal steel and The O.C.
eras.text: As a five-piece the band grew organ, horns and pedal steel around Halstead's songs, and Rolling Stone called the second album stunning. By the fourth the songs were turning up on prime-time TV.

yt: In-store set, Virgin Megastore Hollywood, April 1999
years.p: Singles "Who Do You Love" in June and "Some Kinda Angel" in September; the second scrapes the UK chart at 87.
years.xp: The A.V. Club praised the "subtle and simple, yet surprisingly full-sounding" playing, with organ, horns and pedal steel. 4AD's notes: a group "grown in both confidence and cohesiveness."

years.p: "In Love with a View", "Any Day Will Be Fine" and "Return to Sender" all come off the third album, which 4AD calls Halstead's most ambitious writing yet.

years.h: Halstead's first solo album, Sleeping on Roads
years.p: A side door for the band's main songwriter. The NME later called him Syd Barrett "if he'd ever set foot on a surf board."
A wider, more colorful palette, and two songs, "Billoddity" and "Bluebird of Happiness," end up on the Fox teen drama. Metacritic: 76.

eras.title: Bright songs, then a long pause
eras.text: Goswell made her own record, the band made its sunniest one, and then illness took Goswell off the road and the band stopped.

years.h: Goswell goes solo with Waves Are Universal
years.p: Her first full-length, on 4AD, nine months after Spoon and Rafter and a month after The Sleep Shelter EP.

years.cap: Mojave 3 in a Puzzles Like You press photo, c. 2006
years.h: Puzzles Like You sounds like the Shins, not Slowdive
years.p: The fifth album is upbeat and bright; 4AD's notes say it sits beside [[The Shins|6c8b9855-ba8b-48f9-ac1d-42167f7f7b18]] and [[Band of Horses|07b6020a-c539-4d68-aeef-f159f3befc76]] and is nearly unrecognizable next to the debut.

years.src: Wikipedia: Rachel Goswell · Wikipedia: Mojave 3 · Wikipedia: Neil Halstead
years.h: Labyrinthitis leaves Goswell deaf in one ear
years.p: It also leaves her with chronic tinnitus, and she stops playing and touring with Mojave 3. The band goes on hiatus.
years.xp: Halstead said in 2008 the band was on a break but planned at least one more album. He made Oh! Mighty Engine for Jack Johnson's Brushfire Records instead.

eras.title: One more summer, then Slowdive
eras.text: Mojave 3 came back for a run of shows and talk of new songs. The new songs never came, and the old band did.

years.h: Back onstage, opening for Band of Horses
years.p: On Israeli radio station Kol HaCampus, Halstead says new material is coming and they may record that summer. Nothing follows.

years.cap: Neil Halstead with Mojave 3 at MAO Livehouse, China
years.h: Slowdive reunite, and that ends Mojave 3
years.p: Halstead, Goswell and McCutcheon go back to Slowdive, which ends Mojave 3 for good.

eras.title: Back in print
eras.text: The records went out of print while the reunited Slowdive got more popular than ever. A small label pressed the debut again, and in 2026 4AD remastered the lot.

years.h: Sonic Cathedral presses 500 sea-foam green Ask Me Tomorrows
years.p: The debut's first vinyl since 1995, in a gold-mirrored sleeve with the original art.

years.h: 4AD reissues all five albums, remastered at Abbey Road
years.p: First time on vinyl and CD since their original release, with Colin Gray photographs on a new Ask Me Tomorrow cover and a slipcase box.
years.xp: A Slowdive Facebook post in June confirmed Mojave 3 won't reform for shows; BrooklynVegan noted Slowdive were then on tour across the UK and Europe.
